rationale.todesfall: If your income stops, your family would be short about {gap} per year. A death benefit of {sum} covers this gap for {years} years, until age {endAge}.
rationale.todesfallIncome: A death benefit of {sum} gives your family {years} years to reorganise, until age {endAge}.
rationale.erwerbsunfaehigkeit: If illness leaves you unable to work, you would be short about {gap} per year once salary continuation and sickness benefits end. A pension of {pension} per year from month {months} closes this gap until age {endAge}.
rationale.erwerbsunfaehigkeitNoAmount: If illness leaves you unable to work, a pension of {pension} per year from month {months} replaces part of your income until age {endAge}.
rationale.savings: In retirement you would be short about {gap} per year. Saving {premium} per year in pillar {pillar} builds up money for it until age {endAge}.
rationale.savingsNoAmount: Saving {premium} per year in pillar {pillar} builds up capital for your retirement until age {endAge}.
rationale.savingsTax: You are not yet using the full pillar 3a tax deduction. With {premium} per year in pillar {pillar} you save taxes every year and build capital for retirement, until age {endAge}.
rationale.auszahlungsplan: {capital} becomes a predictable income from age {startAge}, partly guaranteed, partly with a chance of returns.
rationale.kinderversicherung: With {premium} per year you save for your child's start into adult life, with disability cover for the child and premium waiver if something happens to you.
rationale.care: Pax Care is free of charge: CHF 2,000 immediate help and personal support for your loved ones in case of death.

suitability.notApplicable: {product} does not need a suitability check.
suitability.intro: With a fund investment you carry a risk of loss. That is why Pax checks, before the offer, whether the product fits your finances, your goal and your experience. Please answer every question for yourself only, without your partner.

a.title: Financial capacity
a.hint: How much would you like to save per year or invest once?
a.netIncome: Your annual net income after social security deductions
a.netAssets: Your net assets after mortgages and debts
a.savingCapacity: How much can you additionally save per year after all expenses?
a.oneOffCapacity: How much can you invest as a one-off amount?

goal.label: What is the goal of your investment?
goal.minimise_loss: I want to keep the risk of loss as low as possible. High chances of gains matter less to me.
goal.moderate_gains: I accept some risk of loss to have moderate chances of gains.
goal.high_gains: I am prepared to take a high risk of loss for the chance of high gains.

horizon.label: Over what period do you want to save or invest?

knowledge.label: How familiar are you with securities?
knowledge.none: I have no knowledge of or experience with securities yet.
knowledge.knowledge_only: I know about securities but have never bought any.
knowledge.experience: Yes, I have already gained knowledge and experience with securities.
knowledge.expert: Yes, I have a lot of experience and know securities very well.

drawdown.label: Your securities lose 30 % of their value. What do you do?
drawdown.sell_all: I sell everything to avoid an even bigger loss.
drawdown.sell_part: I sell part of them to limit my loss if prices keep falling.
drawdown.hold: I do nothing for now, because I am aware that markets fluctuate.
drawdown.buy_more: I invest more, because I expect a recovery.

d.title: Guaranteed part
d.hint: The guaranteed part of your premium carries no risk of loss and therefore raises your score.
d.none: {product} invests the whole premium in funds, without a guaranteed part.
d.label: Guaranteed share of the premium
